summary: Added synchronous borrowed match-batch delivery across the literal, regex and many-match Search paths, retained immediate delivery for existential file results, and verified output ownership, failure and disposal behavior. The managed boundary measurement preserved all occurrences and reduced sink calls, but did not show a universal wall-clock speedup.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean before W11-S04 implementation; ignored campaign state had W11-S04 active and the scope changes were then introduced.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production, benchmark, test and contract-documentation files changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, package version, publication state or native backend was changed.
implementation.baseline: The compatibility path invokes the sink's single-match operation for every matcher span. Existing existential file-result behavior remains immediate so the first result can terminate the read.
implementation.candidate: The scanner delivers each populated matcher output as one synchronous borrowed IReadOnlyList batch. Built-in occurrence, line and count sinks consume batches synchronously, and SearchManySource materializes rows while the batch is valid.
implementation.ownershipContract: The scanner may clear and reuse a batch after AcceptMatches returns. Consumers crossing an asynchronous or native boundary must copy before returning; the contract document records this rule.
implementation.failurePolicy: Batch-consumer exceptions remain typed as SearchSourceReadException at the scanner boundary, cancellation is preserved, and reader disposal is protected by the existing using scope.
implementation.measurement: Added measure-match-batches with a deterministic 50,000-hit workload, one excluded warmup and seven randomized paired trials. It checks equal occurrence count and coordinate hash while recording timing, allocations and single/batch operation counts.
implementation.nativeBoundary: No native backend is claimed or introduced because none is present in the owning repository; the measured seam is the ownership-explicit integration point for a future native candidate.

scenarios: Dense literal hits arrive as multiple batches and are copied without loss or reordering.
A large regex capture batch preserves every match and both named captures.
An injected batch-bridge failure is typed and the reader is disposed.
An existential sink retains immediate single-match delivery and early read termination.
Repeated batch scans dispose every reader.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,557 total tests, 1,523 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the focused Search suites also passed.

The separate review approved the borrowed-batch ownership contract, immediate existential path, failure/disposal behavior and measured limitation; the exact scope and repository trailers are required for completion.
Dense literal and large capture tests preserve all match data, and the seven-trial measurement reports identical 50,000-occurrence counts and coordinate hashes for baseline and candidate.

The batch is borrowed only during a synchronous consumer call; bridge failure is typed, cancellation remains observable, and repeated-reader tests verify disposal. No native or dangling-memory claim is made.

knownLimitations: The benchmark measures the managed scanner/sink boundary with a deterministic StringReader workload; it is not a native backend or a full filesystem-to-query end-to-end workload.

The current seven-trial candidate median is 1.063x the compatibility baseline, so this scope makes no universal wall-clock throughput claim; the demonstrated benefit is operation-count amortization and an explicit future interop seam.
The batch is synchronous and borrowed. Any future asynchronous or native consumer must copy the spans before returning; this scope does not certify such a consumer.
The final run executed on an x64 host; ARM64 was not emulated or directly measured.
The repository suite retained 34 existing classified skips: 31 expected and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed.
